question_text: What voltage must be applied to a tungsten filament to produce a continuous spectrum of x-rays having a minimum wavelength of 0.09 nm?The unit of the answer is V.
response:
Using the Duane–Hunt law, the minimum (short-wavelength cutoff) of the continuous x-ray spectrum relates to the accelerating voltage by:

$$\lambda_{\min} = \frac{hc}{eV} \quad\Rightarrow\quad V = \frac{hc}{e\,\lambda_{\min}}$$

With $\lambda_{\min} = 0.09\ \text{nm} = 0.09\times10^{-9}\ \text{m}$, $h = 6.626\times10^{-34}\ \text{J·s}$, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\ \text{m/s}$, and $e = 1.602\times10^{-19}\ \text{C}$:

$$V = \frac{(6.626\times10^{-34})(3.0\times10^{8})}{(1.602\times10^{-19})(0.09\times10^{-9})} \approx 1.38\times10^{4}\ \text{V}$$

$$\boxed{1.38\times10^{4}}$$
